scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-04.statement: Field route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, for period 2026-08..09.

F-05.statement: Dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against an SLA of 3.0 days.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/handling problem (slow or templated answers), not a rise in actually-wrong bills, so auto-answering tickets would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced a defect (e.g. in estimate substitution logic) that is generating incorrect bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The AMI/MDMS vendor's nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or became incomplete since August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: The contracted manual meter-reading handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) is delivering incomplete or invalid reads since August, driving estimated/incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Reduced field-reading staffing/capacity is causing missed routes and more estimated reads, as SH-FIELD attributes the problem to staffing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1785 have read_type ACTUAL and 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED, so disputed bills are not concentrated on estimated/substituted reads — a majority (1785 of 3025) are bills built on actual meter reads.

Billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes were recorded in the queried period, which rules out tariff adjustments as a cause of the wrong bills behind the dispute surge. This log is a distinct source from the billing-config import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) referenced by H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.

Route-log shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. roughly 12% of manual-read routes were not completed as scheduled, a plausible source of missing/incomplete reads feeding estimate substitution.

CRM data shows ticket handling is already fast (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) and within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so the dispute surge is not explained by slow or inadequate ticket response — the problem lies upstream in bill correctness, not in response speed.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a three-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late manual-read routes, which produces estimated bills for those customers — this is the Field Operations Manager's own account, not verified data, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive to attribute problems to staffing (contract headcount increase).

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which corroborates the authoritative tariff_change_log result (E-02) already ruling out tariff adjustments as a cause of the dispute surge. As a stakeholder statement it is a claim, not independent verification, but it agrees with the existing authoritative value.

CRM monthly dispute counts show 610 (2026-06) and 590 (2026-07) baseline rising to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09), confirming the surge roughly doubled starting in August as the initial request claimed, but the raw volume trend does not by itself indicate which upstream cause (AMI export, field reads, staffing, rule change, or response handling) is responsible.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative contract clause confirming that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this formalizes the authority already reflected in constraint K-DISPATCH and does not speak to the billing-defect causal chain behind the dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query shows 320 distinct accounts received an estimated bill in the last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (e.g. account AC-20000 on route R-00). This is a snapshot of estimate-substitution scale/spread but does not itself link these accounts to disputes or to a time trend.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 specific routes falling short of completion target, each with a distinct completion value (sample route R-00 at 0.70, well below the 0.95 target). This adds route-level granularity under the aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-03/F-04) but does not itself link these routes to disputed bills, read types, or the staffing explanation (E-05) — no dispute or account-level join is present in this record set.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Customer Service requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Monthly dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August: 610/590 (Jun/Jul) baseline to 1180/1260 (Aug/Sep) (F-06).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 are built on ACTUAL reads vs 1240 ESTIMATED reads, i.e. the majority of disputed bills are not estimate-driven (F-01, F-02).
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (F-04).
Dispute ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA) across 2440 tickets (F-05).
Billing-db tariff change log shows zero rate changes in the queried period (F-03).
problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August (F-06) because a defect in the billing import/validation step is producing incorrect bills for a majority of accounts, including those built on actual (non-estimated) meter reads (F-01, F-02) — ruling out field/AMI read failures as the dominant mechanism — consistent with the supported hypothesis that an August billing import validation rule change introduced the defect (H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT), while tariff changes (F-03) and slow ticket handling (F-05) are ruled out as causes.

This defect causes the billing import + validation step to produce incorrect bills, affecting a majority of accounts with ACTUAL (not just estimated) reads (F-01, F-02).
Tariff rates were not changed (F-03), ruling out tariff adjustments as the cause.

Read-type analysis (E-01) shows disputes are not concentrated on estimated/substituted reads, ruling out field-read and AMI-export failures as the dominant driver despite a real manual-read route completion shortfall (F-04).
Customers receiving incorrect bills file dispute tickets, which are handled within SLA (F-05), so the surge is not a handling-speed problem.
Monthly dispute ticket counts roughly double starting August relative to the Jun/Jul baseline (F-06).
